result.title: PairAudit: Guiding Human Review with Graph Tokens under Distribution Shift
result.summary: Intrusion detectors can confidently misclassify attacks that were not seen during training. Human review can correct these errors, but only a limited number of cases can be checked. Uncertainty-based review may overlook confident errors, while anomaly scores alone do not show whether changing the review plan will correct more errors. We introduce PairAudit to find overlooked errors and improve review under a fixed budget. Its graph tokens capture prediction patterns across connected nodes. Rather than building another predictor through feature aggregation, PairAudit uses unusual relational patterns to uncover potential errors in existing predictions. Human feedback then helps decide whether these findings justify changing review priorities. Experiments across security tasks show that PairAudit corrects more errors on average than uncertainty-based review, including more errors on unseen attacks. These gains account for all review costs and do not require retraining the detector.

AI.brief_summary: PairAudit 面向入侵检测在分布偏移下出现的自信误分类，用图 token 捕捉节点间预测关系中的异常模式来定位被忽视的错误，并在固定预算下借助人工反馈调整复核优先级。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把「关系模式异常」作为筛选高价值证据的准则，并显式权衡复核收益与成本，可能与 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、LOOK/STOP 决策及预算下的推理停止判断形成概念类比，但跨域迁移性需要核查。
